evaluations.rationale:
Candidate-01 meets PoR because it does assignment-specific work rather than restating the selected Spring. The Spring treated the 20 MW floor, assurances, and early-exit recovery as one separable piece worth keeping while holding the rest of S. 5653. This candidate splits the cost title itself and asks which of two rules should govern. On the introduced bill, that split is real. GovInfo's introduced text and contemporaneous BPC, CRS, and Grid Strategies summaries show Section 2107(a) directing FERC to revise the 1994 higher-of policy so computational loads pay both embedded and incremental transmission costs, with no megawatt cutoff, and Section 2107(b) adding a Federal Power Act floor for covered loads of 20 MW or more covering incremental generation, storage, transmission, and distribution, plus assurances and exit recovery. Threshold, cost base, and jurisdiction differ. History is empty, so this is not a replay of a prior selected Autumn or a simple reversal of hold-versus-pass.

The weakness is the text under debate. The selected Spring says the November 9 cloture vote opened debate on a substitute carried by H.R. 2347. Capito, Lee, Whitehouse, and Heinrich released that substitute on November 7. Advancing American Freedom's November 9 reading of Section 2107 says the 20 MW threshold is gone, and secondary summaries say the broader floor now tracks computational-load sites without that cutoff. I could not extract the substitute PDF, so that change is not verified line by line, but it is credible enough that the candidate should have confronted it. Its answerBody presents the 20 MW floor as a live choice Congress must enact before the new Congress convenes. If the substitute dropped the threshold, the next Spring would be asked to choose a rule the pending text no longer offers.

Even on the introduced text, the prompt overstates mutual exclusion. And pricing is a FERC transmission-rate rewrite; the floor is a retail incremental-cost and assurance rule. They can coexist, and choosing one does not settle assurances, exit liability, sub-20 MW loads, or the permitting, tribal, and judicial titles the Spring held the package over. The fork is still genuine and consequential rather than generic, so meetsPor is true. Rank 1 is mandatory because it is the only candidate, not a judgment that the prompt is ready without a text-version correction.

rationale: I verified the candidate's core premise against the introduced S. 5653 text and secondary summaries, then checked whether that premise survives the November 7 substitute that the selected Spring treats as the text under debate. The introduced Section 2107 does pair a size-neutral FERC embedded-plus-incremental transmission rewrite with a 20 MW incremental-cost floor covering generation, storage, transmission, and distribution. That is a real fork, so the candidate shows assignment-specific reasoning and meets PoR. A credible secondary reading of the substitute says the 20 MW threshold was removed; the substitute PDF itself was not extractable here, so that point remains unresolved. The prompt also treats overlapping rules as mutually exclusive and leaves the Spring's non-cost objections outside the question. It is therefore the strongest of one, but only a qualified next Spring input.
